subject: Migration mode selection follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Nova Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@novahealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Migration mode selection follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Nova Health)

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate the context on Nova Health's current LLM usage and the migration drivers. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap:
- Current state: prototypes running on a mix of self-hosted model endpoints and legacy GPU clusters managed by the infra team.
- Primary requirements you called out: strict PHI controls, predictable latency for clinical workflows, and a clear migration timeline with rollback paths.
- Constraints: procurement timeline ~Q3, security questionnaire (SOC2) in flight, and a small but growing inference footprint today.

Deployment mode considerations (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, simple integration, and pay-as-you-go — but may require additional contractual language for PHI/data residency.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools + SLAs — good fit if you want predictable throughput and data isolation without managing infra.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): highest control for regulation — recommended if you must fully isolate inference and host keys in your KMS/HSM.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) next week with your infra/security lead + our infra eng (Markus) to validate the Dedicated vs Private feasibility.
2) Share our DPA + SOC2 summary and a draft MSA (I attached the DPA and a short deck on deployment options).
3) High-level mutual action plan: target pilot on Dedicated capacity in Q3, with a Private/VPC path if procurement requires it.

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tue 5/4 10:00–10:45am PT or Wed 5/5 9:00–9:45am PT. Which works best?

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (overview), redwood-dpa-v1.docx (DPA draft).

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your procurement/security timelines.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Subject: Re: Migration mode selection follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Nova Health)

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

1) Data residency & PHI: our legal team is strongly leaning toward either Dedicated capacity with customer-managed VPC peering or a Private VPC/on-prem deployment. Hosted public API will require stronger contractual safeguards and may add time to procurement.

2) Latency: clinical paths need ~100–200ms p95 for short prompt flows; for batch workloads we can tolerate higher latency but prefer cost savings.

3) Migration origin: most of our traffic is currently routed through an existing LLM API provider (third-party SaaS), with several experimental models on a small on-prem GPU cluster for PII-sensitive workloads. We need a migration plan that lets us pilot with non-critical traffic first.

Attached our internal architecture sketch (nova-architecture.pdf) and a brief procurement note.

We can do Wed 5/5 9:00am PT for the technical deep-dive — I will invite our infra lead (Raj) and procurement (procurement@novahealth.com).

Two immediate asks before the call:
- Can you share a short note on the Dedicated capacity network model (VPC peering, routing, KMS integration)?
- Any examples of customers who migrated from a hosted LLM API to Dedicated/Private?

Cheers,
Sarah
Director, Engineering — Nova Health
sarah.lee@novahealth.com

Attachments: nova-architecture.pdf

Subject: Re: Migration mode selection follow-up — Migration plan and Dedicated network model

Hi Sarah (and team),

Great — confirmed for Wed 5/5 at 9:00am PT. I added procurement on this thread so Markus can surface commercial and network details during the call.

High-level answers to your asks (short form — we'll go deeper on the call):
- Dedicated network model: we offer VPC peering and private link options. For Dedicated we can peer into your VPC and route inference traffic over private links; KMS integration supports bring-your-own-key via supported KMS providers (we'll confirm specifics for your KMS).
- Migration examples: we recently helped a healthcare analytics customer migrate from a third-party LLM API to Redwood Dedicated over an 8-week pilot — started with non-PHI traffic, validated latency/SLOs, then expanded to production and enabled VPC peering for sensitive traffic. I will share a short case study on the call.

Proposed shortened MAP for pilot: 
- Week 0: alignment + security checklist (we'll provide SOC2 artifacts and DPA).
- Week 1–2: Dedicated pilot provisioning + sample workload run (non-PHI) + latency/cost baseline.
- Week 3–6: performance tuning (batching, quantization), KV/prefix cache config, and integration adjustments.
- Week 6–8: production rollout for selected flows and handoff to your platform team.

I've attached the DPA draft again and a short one-pager on deployment options. I'll also post the HubSpot MAP and DocuSign placeholder after the call.

Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Migration mode selection follow-up — infra notes for today

Sarah / team,

Quick infra notes to add before the call: 
- If Nova is migrating from a hosted LLM API, the low-friction path is Dedicated capacity with traffic mirroring during pilot (split-traffic) so you can compare outputs and latency without fully cutting over.
- For legacy GPU clusters: we typically map model compatibility (FP16/INT8) and KV cache expectations; if you self-host certain models we can run a staged hybrid where sensitive prompts stay on-cluster and non-sensitive on Dedicated.
- Ops tune: expect turning on continuous batching + prefix KV cache to reduce token costs — we'll run a quick benchmark to show typical p95 improvements.

I will cover the network/VPC peering and KMS details in the call and share a short diagram.

—Markus
